checkpoints.name: reset_held
checkpoints.description: Reset is still asserted; PC is at 0 and the first instruction is presented on the instr bus.

checkpoints.name: after_first_addi
checkpoints.description: First ADDI (x1 <- 5) has retired; PC has advanced to 0x4 and x1 holds 5.

checkpoints.name: after_add_and_sub
checkpoints.description: ADD x3, x1, x2 and SUB x4, x2, x1 have both retired. x3 = 12 (0x0C), x4 = 2.

checkpoints.name: after_lw
checkpoints.description: SW (mem[0] <- 12) has executed and LW (x5 <- mem[0]) has retired. x5 = 12.

checkpoints.name: branch_taken_pc_advance
checkpoints.description: BEQ x3, x5, +8 is taken (x3 == x5 == 12). PC jumps from 0x18 directly to 0x20, skipping the ADDI x6 at 0x1C.

checkpoints.name: after_second_add
checkpoints.description: ADD x9, x7, x8 has retired. x7 = 10, x8 = 11, x9 = 21 (0x15).

checkpoints.name: jal_self_loop
checkpoints.description: All 14 dynamic instructions executed; JAL x0, 0 is in flight and PC has stabilised at 0x38.

checkpoints.name: datapath_structure
checkpoints.description: In NetCrux, the CPU top is assembled from an instruction memory and a register file — the two blocks a single-cycle datapath is built around.

cross_tool_deep_links.name: register_value_to_datapath
cross_tool_deep_links.source_action: having read a register's value change in the waveform as instructions execute, cross-probe that register to the structure that writes it
cross_tool_deep_links.expected_target_state: the register file module is shown, with the write-address, write-data and write-enable paths that the executing instruction drives — connecting the value you saw change in time to the datapath that changed it
